claim: Across three meta-analyses, text and picture placed together beat separated, but the pooled size is falling (Ginns 2006 d 0.85 on 50 studies, spatial and temporal pooled; Wang 2016 retention d 0.48, transfer d 0.39; Schroeder and Cenkci 2018 g 0.63 on 58 comparisons, n = 2426, abstract now read first-hand). No bias-corrected size was found; the full papers' bias checks could not be opened.
agent_test: Same task, same tokens: facts and their referents in one line (integrated) vs facts in a header block and referents in a footer (separated). Measure accuracy over many items and seeds.

claim: Ginns 2006 size clash resolved in part: the abstract says 50 independent studies that pool spatial AND temporal contiguity, and the quoted d = 0.85 (95% CI 0.68 to 1.02) belongs to that pooled set. The 0.72 on 37 effects is most likely the spatial-only subset (inference, not confirmed). Cite 0.85 only as 'spatial plus temporal'. Chandler and Sweller 1992 is still unopened.
agent_test: None. Bibliographic fix: open Ginns 2006 full text.

claim: The split-attention effect is not universal in humans: Cammeraat 2020 (Exp 2) found no effect on retention, transfer or effort; Beege 2019 Exp 1 (N=98) found separated not worse than integrated; Schmidt-Weigand 2010 and Florax and Ploetzner 2010 are named non-replications. New in the gap pass: Beege 2019 Exp 1 planned contrast integrated vs separated was null (retention p = .51, transfer p = .15, N = 98); Florax and Ploetzner 2010 (N = 165) found the effect for retention only and credited text segmentation, not nearness; Zhang's 2022 (N = 122) and 2024 (N = 146) tests were null while 2023 (N = 129) confirmed; Jarodzka 2015 found the split format more efficient when the extra text was irrelevant.
agent_test: Treat every layout rule as a hypothesis: run integrated vs separated at equal tokens and keep it only if it wins (G7).

claim: Element interactivity moderates the effect: strong with complex material (d 0.78), weak and not significant with simple material (d 0.28), and extraneous load matters mostly when intrinsic load is already high. The 0.78/0.28 pair is second-hand through Beege 2019. The d 0.78 (complex) vs 0.28 (simple, p > 0.05) split is quoted from Ginns 2006 by Beege 2019; Ginns full text was not opened.
agent_test: Gate by difficulty: apply input restructuring only on multi-element items; on easy items compare plain vs restructured and expect no gain.

claim: Integration helps only when the sources are unintelligible alone. If text restates a self-contained diagram (or the same words come as both text and audio), integration or duplication adds load (redundancy effect).
agent_test: Prompt A: original statement plus a restatement; Prompt B: original only. Equal tokens by padding B with neutral task-relevant detail. Expect restatement to hurt when the original is already clear.

claim: Split attention can be cut without physical integration: audio instead of on-screen text (F(2,31)=7.74 and 10.66, N=34) and colour-coding (N=16, F(1,13)=7.17 on multiple choice). Both are single small studies of trade apprentices.
agent_test: Use consistent labels or ids that tie each fact to its referent (a text-only analogue of colour-coding). Compare against unlabelled at equal tokens.

claim: Cognitive load mediates only a small share of the human effect: format did not change a secondary-task load measure in Cierniak 2012 Study 1 (N=103); extraneous load mediated 8 to 16 percent. Wang 2016 shows only a small rated-load shift (d -0.24); the Kalyuga 1999 load difference was marginal. Pouw 2019 (abstract only) found distance changes process, not learning. Schroeder 2020 reviewed 41 comparisons: load measures largely do not support the extraneous-load explanation and integrated designs did not clearly change any load measure; the author proposes germane or integrative processing instead.
agent_test: Do not build a load meter for the agent from this theory; measure outcome accuracy, not a load proxy.

claim: Telling learners to mentally integrate separated sources closes most of the gap (N=87; recall d=0.77, comprehension d=0.94 vs no strategy), at the size of the imagination effect.
agent_test: Add an instruction to first link each fact to its referent in one line before reasoning; compare with no instruction at equal tokens.

claim: Adding irrelevant text to a problem sharply lowers LLM accuracy: GSM-IC (no more than 18 percent of solved base problems solved for all distractor types), GSM-NoOp (drops up to 65 percent), and padding with unrelated text (mean accuracy 0.92 to 0.68 at 3,000 tokens). Newer models still lose: GSM-DC (2025) Grok-3-Beta step accuracy 43% to 19% and GPT-4.1 26% to 2% from 1 to 15 irrelevant items at depth 5; GSM-Plus (2024) human drop -2.05% vs GPT-4 8.23%.
agent_test: Input hygiene test: same items with and without a planted inert sentence; then with code-based removal of non-task text.

claim: Length alone, with no distractor content, also hurts: Du 2025 (13.9 to 85 percent drops with whitespace or masked tokens, 5 models) and Levy 2024. But Adapala 2025 found its long-control condition not significantly different from control (0.82 vs 0.85, p=.45), and 3 of 5 models were at floor there. Gap pass: RULER shows GPT-4 losing about 3 points from 4K to 32K (96.6 to 93.2) and 15 points by 128K; Llama3.1 70B 96.5 to 94.8 at 32K and 66.6 at 128K; so at agent lengths of 5K to 30K the length-alone loss is small for strong models. Still contested for clean, task-relevant text because RULER is mostly filler.
agent_test: Cap context at what the step needs; test one long-but-clean prompt against a short one at equal task content.

claim: Where information sits matters: accuracy is U-shaped by position of the relevant passage (drop over 20 points for GPT-3.5-Turbo; worst case below closed-book 56.1 percent), and premise order matching the proof order matters (drops over 30 percent).
agent_test: Put the question and key facts first and last; test premise order matching the solution order versus shuffled.

claim: A prompt instruction to ignore irrelevant information helps but does not cure: Shi 2023 code-davinci-002 chain-of-thought micro accuracy 72.4 to 77.8 and overall macro 6.0 to 15.0. In GSM-NoOp, more shots did not close the gap.
agent_test: Test the one-line instruction at equal tokens; expect small gain on strong models.

claim: Filter-then-answer works: S2A rewrite (factual QA with opinions 62.8 to 80.3 percent; GSM-IC 51.7 to 61.3), recite-then-answer (Mistral-7B GSM8K at 26,250 tokens 35.5 to 66.7), and question-aware compression (up to +21.4 percent with about 4x fewer tokens).
agent_test: S1 UNDERSTAND with code-side input hygiene vs model-side rewrite vs none, at equal total tokens including the rewrite call.

claim: Not all extra text is equally harmful: related-but-wrong passages hurt most (-25 percent with one distractor), random unrelated documents sometimes helped (up to +35 percent); similar padding hurts more than dissimilar; hop-recall drop correlated with task similarity (r 0.35 to 0.42). Shi 2023 breakdown: same-topic sentences, shared role names and in-range numbers are the hardest in arithmetic reasoning too, so the near-miss pattern is not limited to retrieval QA.
agent_test: Seed a prompt with near-miss distractors vs random distractors; first drop the near-miss ones.

claim: Agent loops benefit from trimming history: observation masking (keep last 10 turns) cut cost 41 to 57% in 4 of 5 setups with solve rate equal within CIs (Lindenbauer 2025, SWE-bench Verified; Qwen3-Coder 53.4 raw, 54.8 masked, 53.8 summary), and ACON compression cut peak tokens. Boundary: Gemini 2.5 Flash with thinking fell from 40.4 raw to 36.4 masked and 31.4 summarised, and summaries lengthened runs (+15% turns vs masking). Software-engineering tool output only.
agent_test: Compare full history vs masked old tool outputs vs LLM summary at equal token budget on our own multi-step tasks.

claim: Spreading one instruction across turns is a machine analogue of separated sources: 15 LLMs, 200,000+ simulations, mean drop 39 percent, visible even in two turns. Single study; reliability loss dominates aptitude loss.
agent_test: Give all facts in a single message vs revealed in shards; keep shards out of S3 attempts (each attempt a fresh full context).

claim: Layout is never neutral: meaning-preserving format changes shift accuracy up to 76 points (LLaMA-2-13B), median 6.4 for GPT-3.5 over 320 formats. A single A/B layout comparison proves little. Voronov 2024 (21 models, 4 datasets) agrees: poor templates drop strong models to chance and standard deviations reach 35% of the mean, so method gaps smaller than template spread are not interpretable.
agent_test: Any layout test needs many formats and many items; report spread, not one pair.

claim: Contrary boundary: in a multimodal benchmark, separating question text and options from the image evidence raised accuracy (open VLMs 41.32 to 50.97; thinking models only +2.10). Integration is not always better, and the gain shrinks for stronger reasoners.
agent_test: Where sources have different modalities or jobs, test separated vs merged; gain should shrink on stronger models.

claim: Still no study found that tests the classic integrated vs separated contrast in text-only LLMs under the split-attention name (two search passes; the second pass had its web quota spent and APIs rate-limited, so the negative is weak). Nearest analogue: premise order, where using facts in the order they are needed beats a shuffled order by 20 to 40 points (Chen 2024).
agent_test: Run it ourselves: the first direct test (see K01 test) is a gap worth filling.

claim: Cognitive-load-framed LLM benchmarks show accuracy falling as extraneous load rises: Adapala 2025 (Gemini slope -0.003 per percent load, p<0.001; GPT-4o trend p=.07, 32 percent of outputs truncated), CogniLoad (22 models, steepest decline between N=20 and 50), ToolLoad (exponential decay, k 0.034 to 0.088). Heterogeneous designs; only 2 of 5 Adapala models informative.
agent_test: Spend more checking budget when a problem has many distractor facts or tools; budget by difficulty (G12).

claim: Distraction has a mechanical component: tokens seen earlier get higher probability (entrainment heads, Niu 2025), and splitting context into separately encoded pieces raises attention entropy and degrades output (Zhang 2025). Each is one mechanistic study.
agent_test: Not testable at the scaffold level; informative only as a prior for why clean inputs help.

claim: Prompts crowded with extra tasks and clutter can break safety training (reported up to 99.99 percent attack success). Seen only in search snippets.
agent_test: Not an accuracy claim; do not use until the paper is opened.

claim: Founding numbers of Chandler and Sweller 1992 are not in hand: the paper was never opened, and its effect is known only second-hand through Sweller 1994 and Kalyuga 1999. Second attempt in the gap pass also failed (publisher 403, ERIC lists no record).
agent_test: None; open the paper or a text that reports its experiments.

claim: Strong reasoning models still lose accuracy to inert or near-miss clauses, and extra thinking does not fix it: o1-preview -17.5 points on GSM-NoOp (o1-mini -29.1, GPT-4o -32.0); Claude Opus 4 falls from near 100% to about 85 to 90% as reasoning lengthens on counting with distractors; DeepSeek R1 70% to 30% at five distractors; Cats triggers raise R1 error 4.50% vs 1.50% baseline. Scale differs by task: Du 2025 saw only 3.8 to 8.5 point drops for Claude and Gemini on GSM8K. No clean 2026 measure on the newest models.
agent_test: Insert 1, 3 and 5 inert clauses and 1, 3 and 5 near-miss clauses into our own tasks; compare raw, code-filtered and 'ignore this' conditions at equal tokens on the current model.

claim: Using facts in the order they are needed matters: shuffling relevant premises costs 20 to 30 points for GPT-4-turbo and over 40 for weaker models on logic (Chen 2024); context before the question beats question-first by about 14.7 points over 21 open models (Ok and Lee 2026), halved with chain-of-thought. Any integrated-vs-separated test must hold use-order fixed in both arms.
agent_test: Within each layout arm, fix the order of facts to match the solution order; run a third arm that shuffles it to size the order effect separately.

claim: Rule density is a budget: with 10 to 500 instructions in one prompt, even the best 2025 models reach only about 68% at 500; reasoning models hold near-perfect until a threshold of roughly 100 to 250, others decay linearly or exponentially, and earlier instructions are followed better. One synthetic task.
agent_test: Measure adherence to our G1-G12 list when all are in the system prompt vs only the ones relevant to the current state.

claim: Length from clean-ish context is a small cost at agent lengths for strong models but a large one at depth: GPT-4 96.6 to 93.2 (4K to 32K) and 81.2 at 128K; multi-hop QA loses 0.245 to 0.270 exact match from 256 to 2048 padded tokens while single-span QA loses 0.025 to 0.065 (Dhara 2026). Hard, multi-step questions are where extra text costs most, which matches the element-interactivity moderator.
agent_test: Split our tasks by number of dependent steps; compare trimmed vs untrimmed context for each bucket. Prediction: trimming helps most in the multi-step bucket.

claim: The first human study of the effect sets the benchmark but is not in hand, and the bias-corrected human size is unknown: the only first-hand pooled figures are g 0.63 (58 comparisons) and d 0.85 CI 0.68 to 1.02 (50 studies, spatial plus temporal, second-hand CI). Treat the human analogy as hypothesis-generating.
agent_test: None. Needs full texts of Chandler and Sweller 1992, Ginns 2006 and Schroeder and Cenkci 2018 (funnel plot or trim-and-fill).
